ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a table with 15 columns. The entries are arranged in a triangular row pattern: row 1 has 1 in column 1; row 2 has 2, 3 in columns 1–2; row 3 has 4, 5, 6 in columns 1–3; row 4 has 7, 8, 9, 10 in columns 1–4; row 5 has 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 in columns 1–5. Ellipses indicate the pattern continues, and the bottom visible row contains 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, ..., 120, ending in column 15. Reasoning: Since the numbers 1 through 120 are used and 120 = 15·16/2, there are 15 triangular rows. Row r contains r consecutive numbers and starts at T_{r-1}+1, where T_n = n(n+1)/2. Thus the entry in row r, column j is T_{r-1}+j, for r >= j. Column j therefore contains entries from rows j through 15. To compare neighboring columns, column j has one extra top entry in row j, equal to T_{j-1}+j = T_j. For each of the remaining rows j+1 through 15, the entry in column j+1 is exactly 1 larger than the entry in column j. There are 15-j such rows. Hence S_{j+1}-S_j = (15-j) - T_j. Compute signs: for j=1, 14-1=13 > 0; for j=2, 13-3=10 > 0; for j=3, 12-6=6 > 0; for j=4, 11-10=1 > 0; for j=5, 10-15=-5 < 0. So the column sums increase through column 5 and then begin decreasing. Therefore the largest sum is in column 5.
